principles: One shared admissibility vocabulary and evaluator owns proof interpretation.
Caller-writable metadata must never become proof by naming alone.
Legacy evidence remains readable but is not silently promoted to strong proof.
Warn-mode diagnostics must precede broad hard-fail enforcement.
Every proof rejection needs stable reason codes and remediation hints.
drivers: Close recurring proof-looking metadata spoof surfaces.
Reduce future one-off evidence bug fixes by centralizing contract checks.
Keep local development usable while hardening production proof consumers.
Satisfy the user request to execute M2-M7 fully with strong verification.

options.name: A: shared admissibility contract with staged warn-to-enforce integration
pros: Reuses B-0985 registry instead of forking logic.
Allows focused tests for reserved keys, semantic binding, legacy classification, handoff, and gate diagnostics.
Reduces false-block risk by starting warn-mode and enforcing high-risk paths last.
cons: Requires touching several core gate seams and writing a broader regression suite.
May take multiple review rounds because failures in one seam can stale evidence elsewhere.

options.name: B: per-gate hardening patches without shared integration
pros: Each fix can be smaller at first.
Less immediate refactor pressure on shared core.
cons: Repeats the same bug class across gates.
Makes proof behavior harder to audit.
Does not satisfy the plan goal of a single admissibility contract.

options.name: C: enforce-only switch over the B-0985 classifier
cons: High false-block risk because metadata sanitization, semantic binding, legacy labeling, and handoff class split are not ready.
Could break old evidence readability and normal local development.

chosen: A: shared admissibility contract with staged warn-to-enforce integration
rationale: Choose staged shared integration because the bug class is systemic: spoofable metadata, incomplete digest binding, stale/legacy evidence, and local handoff overclaim need one contract and one vocabulary. Warn-mode lets gates expose inadmissible evidence before hard failures, while M7 can enforce only after M2-M6 regression coverage exists.

preMortem.scenario: Reserved proof-key sanitizer strips ordinary user metadata.
preMortem.trigger: A broad key match removes benign fields that only contain words like proof or authority.
preMortem.consequence: Existing commands lose display/audit metadata or users see surprising compatibility breaks.
preMortem.mitigation: Sanitize only a narrow registered reserved-key set and add ordinary metadata survival tests.

preMortem.scenario: Semantic binding tests pass but a gate still consumes an unbound field.
preMortem.trigger: A gate reads a field not listed in the canonical payload helper.
preMortem.consequence: A future edit to reason/verdict/story/material can bypass digest checks.
preMortem.mitigation: Create canonical payload helpers and adversarial tests that mutate every gate-consumed semantic field.

preMortem.scenario: Warn-mode diagnostics become noisy and hide real blockers.
preMortem.trigger: Every legacy or local diagnostic artifact emits long warnings in normal flows.
preMortem.consequence: Hosts ignore warnings or users perceive the system as broken.
preMortem.mitigation: Classify warnings by consumer/claim and only surface concise scope/reason/remediation rows at gate reports.

preMortem.scenario: Enforce mode blocks old audit evidence needed for history.
preMortem.trigger: Legacy artifacts lacking new fields are treated as malformed instead of legacy-readable.
preMortem.consequence: Historical stories become impossible to inspect or migrate.
preMortem.mitigation: Implement legacy scopes and dry-run migration diagnostics before enabling hard-fail gates.

preMortem.scenario: Handoff outputs accidentally imply productionDone after adding proof refs.
preMortem.trigger: A host sees an admissibleProofRef field and treats it as a completed production claim without gate consumption.
preMortem.mitigation: Handoff summaries must split context/candidate/diagnostic/proofRef and keep productionDone=false unless a matching gate consumes a verified receipt.
